claims.claim: The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out of the Sun.
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084 'Origin of Light' (svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084, fetched); Mitalas & Sills 1992, ApJ 401, 759 (ADS scan, both pages read; DOI 10.1086/172103 checked on Crossref); NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml, fetched)
claims.note: SVS: 'Over the course of 40,000 years it will be absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface' and 'Over tens of thousands of years, the photons travel a "drunken walk"'. MS92: t_d = 1.7 x 10^5 yr to the inner edge of the convection zone; the common 3e3-3e4 yr estimates are 'much too short'. MSFC: 'about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. Every cited figure is >= 4e4 yr, so 'tens of thousands, maybe far more' holds as a lower bound; the MS92/MSFC figures stop at ~0.7 R, and the convective remainder only adds time. Stix 2003 not read, but nothing rests on it.

claims.claim: Hook as heard by a viewer who swipes at second two: 'The energy in the sunlight on your skin...' over the Sun-Earth shot (Earth labelled 'not to scale', pulse crossing the gap).
claims.note: By 2.0 s the VO has reached 'The energy in the sunlight on your'; 'skin' ends 2.35 s, the full sentence 6.5 s. Nothing false is stated or implied at that point, and the full first sentence is a lower bound every cited source supports. The script avoids the popular false form ('the light/photon is 100,000 years old'). No numeric tag is on screen in the first two seconds.

claims.claim: The trip from the Sun to you took eight minutes.
claims.source_checked: NASA NSSDC Sun Fact Sheet (fetched: mean distance 149.6e6 km, min 147.1, max 152.1; radius 695,700 km); CODATA 2022 c via physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?c (fetched: 299 792 458 m/s exact); NASA SVS 11084
claims.note: (149.6e6 - 0.6957e6) km / c = 496.7 s = 8 min 17 s; perihelion/aphelion give 488-505 s (8.1-8.4 min), +/-1.7% as stated. SVS: 'Light takes eight minutes to travel the 93 million miles from the sun to Earth.' IAU 2012 B2 not reachable, but the NSSDC mean distance suffices.

claims.claim: Getting out was the slow part.
claims.note: 8 minutes against >= 40,000 years. Minor: SOURCES entry 3 says '8 minutes against more than 1e5 years', which conflicts with its own SVS lower figure of 4e4; suggest '>= 4e4 years' there. Does not affect the spoken line.

claims.claim: But it is not the same light.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; NASA SVS 11084
claims.note: Read with the next two lines it means a different kind of light: MSFC says the energy diffuses outward 'by radiation (mostly gamma-rays and x-rays)' and 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'; the outer 30% is crossed by convective flows, not radiation. SVS: photons 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly'. Supported either way it is read.

claims.claim: Deep inside, it travels mostly as X-rays.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior' (fetched); CODATA 2022 Wien constant via physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?bwien (fetched: 2.897 771 955e-3 m K); recomputed SOURCES' figures
claims.note: The cited source says 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays', not 'mostly X-rays'. The narrowing rests on a derivation whose arithmetic checks (hc/(b/T) = 6.4, 3.0, 0.86 keV at 15, 7, 2 MK; 2.82 kT = 3.6, 1.7, 0.49 keV) and the physics is right, but two premises have no A2 citation: (a) that ~0.5-6 keV photons are X-rays (the X-ray band edges), and (b) that the interior radiation field is near-blackbody at the local temperature. A1/A3 fail as written. Fix either way: (1) add to SOURCES entry 4 an A2 citation (agency page or textbook with edition) stating the X-ray energy range (~0.1-100 keV) and the near-blackbody interior radiation field, and have it re-checked; or (2) change the line to match MSFC, e.g. 'Deep inside, it travels as X-rays and gamma rays.' (requires re-render/re-align).

claims.claim: It leaves as sunlight.
claims.note: MSFC: the core reactions 'release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'.

claims.claim: The energy is ancient.
claims.note: Qualitative; >= 40,000 years (SVS) to ~1e6 years (MSFC) fairly reads as ancient.

claims.claim: Its last eight minutes were the trip to you.
claims.source_checked: as claim 3 (NSSDC, CODATA c, NASA SVS)
claims.note: ~8.3 min photosphere to Earth; SVS 'Light takes eight minutes to travel ... from the sun to Earth'.

claims.claim: Sun-Earth shot (start and end): Earth labelled 'not to scale' while visible; a bright pulse crosses the gap.
claims.source_checked: src/shorts/age-of-sunlight/index.tsx; NASA NSSDC Sun Fact Sheet
claims.note: Drawn: Sun r 110, Earth r 24, 600 units apart. Real: Sun/Earth radius ratio 109.2 (drawn 4.6, so Earth ~24x too big); distance ~215 solar radii (drawn 5.5, ~39x too close). Code comment '~25x too big, ~40x too close' is right, and the label is tied to Earth's opacity, so A6 is met. The pulse makes no timed or numeric claim.

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES / surface to your skin / not to scale
claims.note: Photosphere to Earth 496.7 s mean (8.1-8.4 min over the year); 'surface' is the right endpoint.

claims.claim: 10,000+ YEARS / energy, core to surface / not to scale (shown while the interior cutaway is up)
claims.source_checked: as claim 1; index.tsx timing (tag from 'slow' to 'ancient'+48 frames, same as the cutaway)
claims.note: A true lower bound under every cited figure (SVS 4e4 core to surface; MS92 1.7e5; MSFC ~1e6). Conservative relative to the spoken 'tens of thousands', not contradictory. The cutaway's 'not to scale' is on screen for its whole duration.

claims.claim: THE ENERGY / 10,000+ years getting out
claims.note: Same lower bound as claim 12.

claims.claim: THE TRIP / 8 minutes to you / not to scale
claims.note: Shown over the Sun-Earth shot, whose Earth also carries 'not to scale'.

claims.claim: Cutaway zones: rings at 0.25 and 0.7 of the Sun's radius; rotating dashed convection cells between 0.7 and the surface.
claims.note: MSFC: core is 'the innermost 25%'; radiative zone 'from 25% of the distance to the surface to 70%'; convection zone 'the outermost 30%', where 'convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface'. Christensen-Dalsgaard et al. 1991 (0.713 R) only checked on Crossref (doi:10.1086/170441, title/authors/volume match); nothing on screen depends on it.

claims.claim: A random-walk path from the centre to the 0.7 ring, with short sideways strokes along it (re-emission).
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084; NASA MSFC; Mitalas & Sills 1992; index.tsx
claims.note: SVS: photons 'travel a "drunken walk," zigzagging their way from atom to atom', 'absorbed ... and emitted repeatedly'. MSFC: photons 'bounce from particle to particle through the radiative zone'. Code scales the walk by its furthest excursion so no leg passes 0.7 R. Step size and count are schematic and labelled not to scale (MS92 mean step 0.090 cm, 1.0e25 steps).

claims.claim: Path colour from violet toward pale yellow by log temperature: 15 MK at r=0, 7 MK at 0.25 R, 2 MK at 0.7 R, 5,700 K at surface; ~10% of the way at 0.25 R, ~26% at 0.7 R.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; index.tsx tint(); recomputed
claims.note: MSFC: centre 'about 15,000,000 C', radiative zone 'falls from 7,000,000 C to about 2,000,000 C', surface '5,700 K'. ln(15/7)/ln(15e6/5700) = 0.097; ln(7.5)/ln(2632) = 0.256. Matches. Hue is schematic and makes no numeric claim on screen.

claims.claim: A fan of five yellow rays leaving the surface.
claims.note: Energy 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'. Shown on 'It leaves as sunlight.'

claims.claim: The energy in sunlight took at least tens of thousands of years to get out of the Sun
claims.note: Lowest cited figure 40,000 yr (SVS); MS92 (peer-reviewed) explicitly rejects the 3e3-3e4 yr estimates as 'much too short'. 'At least tens of thousands' is supported. Matches index.tsx title.

claims.claim: Sunlight reaches you about eight minutes after leaving the Sun's surface.
claims.note: 496.7 s mean from the photosphere.

claims.claim: But the energy it carries spent tens of thousands of years, maybe far more, getting out.
claims.note: Same as the spoken hook.

claims.claim: Estimates include about 40,000 years (NASA SVS), 170,000 (Mitalas & Sills 1992) and about a million (NASA Marshall).
claims.source_checked: NASA SVS 11084; Mitalas & Sills 1992 (ADS scan); NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'
claims.note: SVS '40,000 years'; MS92 't_d = 1.7 x 10^5 yr'; MSFC 'about a million years'. All three quoted figures match their sources.

claims.claim: The slow part is diffusing out through the Sun's dense interior; near the surface, convection carries it up quickly.
claims.source_checked: NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior'; Mitalas & Sills 1992
claims.note: MSFC: energy 'diffuses outward by radiation' through the radiative zone (20 to 0.2 g/cm3) and convection carries heat 'quite rapidly to the surface'; MS92: convective crossing time 'very much shorter' than diffusion. 'Near the surface' is loose for a zone 30% of the radius (~200,000 km) deep; optional tightening: 'in the outer 30%'.

claims.claim: Deep inside, it travels mostly as X-rays. It leaves as sunlight.
claims.note: Same issue as claim 6: MSFC says 'mostly gamma-rays and x-rays'; the narrowing to 'mostly X-rays' rests on an uncited X-ray band definition and blackbody assumption. Apply the same fix as claim 6 (add the A2 citation, or change to 'as X-rays and gamma rays'). 'It leaves as sunlight' is confirmed (claim 7).

claims.claim: Description source list: Mitalas & Sills 1992 (doi:10.1086/172103); NASA Marshall Solar Interior; NASA SVS Origin of Light; NASA Sun Fact Sheet; CODATA 2022 speed of light.
claims.source_checked: Crossref record for 10.1086/172103 (title, authors, ApJ 401, 759, 1992 match); each URL fetched
claims.note: All are A2 (peer-reviewed with DOI, NASA agency pages, CODATA). Covers every figure in the description. If claim 6/24 is fixed by adding a citation, add it here too (E4).

claims.claim: Illustrated animation; marked shots are not to scale.
claims.note: Both non-to-scale shots (Sun-Earth, cutaway) carry 'not to scale' on screen for their whole duration.
